description: ALAB SPACE AGENCY (ASA) is an independent students initiative focused on space exploration, aerospace engineering, science, and technology. Participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Ben Guerir, Morocco, ASA aims to transform scientific knowledge and NASA's open data into innovative solutions for the future of space exploration.
summary:
MUZN ASA is an educational game created by ALAB SPACE AGENCY, a student team from Lycée Mohammed VI d’Excellence de Benguerir (LM6E) in Morocco. MUZN ASA turns the work of planning space missions into a fun practical learning adventure.

The game takes ideas from NASAs mission design tools. Uses public NASA GMAT data. MUZN ASA takes players through every step of planning a space mission. Players set mission goals build a spacecraft, pick systems look at orbit options check engineering limits and run mission simulations. The game covers the four main mission stages: Launch, Space, Ground and User.

By linking science ideas with engineering choices MUZN ASA solves the Space Mission Design Game challenge in a clear hands‑on way. The game pushes players to think about systems solve problems and stay curious, about science. MUZN ASA  also shows how many different decisions together decide if a space mission can work and succeed.
details:
MUZN ASA is a browser-based educational game that introduces users to the process of designing and managing a scientific space mission. It currently features an uncrewed spacecraft mission in Earth orbit allowing players to experience how scientific objectives and engineering decisions are connected.

The experience guides users through a mission-design workflow. Players define their mission objectives select a mission architecture and launch options, configure spacecraft components and evaluate the engineering consequences of their choices. The spacecraft design includes systems such as power, propulsion, communications, thermal control, attitude control, avionics and scientific instruments. The platform evaluates parameters, including mass, power consumption, available energy, cost, data generation, communications capacity, reliability and mission risk. Users can then explore parameters run a simplified mission simulation and review the results through a mission report.

The project is designed to make aerospace engineering concepts more accessible and understandable. Its main benefit is that learners do not simply read about spacecraft engineering: they interact with the design process make decisions and observe how constraints influence mission feasibility. Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity, systems thinking, problem-solving and interest in space science and engineering particularly, among students.

MUZN ASA was developed as a web application using Lovable with React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS for its frontend. It combines interface components, engineering calculations, data visualizations and a simplified orbital simulation. Its orbital reference section draws on available NASA General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) tutorial parameters. These are used as references; MUZN ASA does not run the GMAT software itself or claim to reproduce its full numerical accuracy. No dedicated physical hardware is required.

The projects creative approach is to bring stages of mission planning together in one interactive learning environment. Than presenting isolated aerospace facts it connects spacecraft configuration, resource management orbital concepts and mission evaluation into a coherent experience. The design was guided by accessibility, scientific clarity, usability and the need to represent engineering trade-offs without overwhelming beginners.

Through MUZN ASA we aim to turn the complexity of space mission design into an opportunity to learn, experiment and think like a mission-design team.
